title: Example apps declare no `engines.protocol` range — ADR-0087's compatibility check is skipped on the templates users copy
body:
Newly visible after #4084 unblocked boot-phase logging. Booting `examples/app-todo` prints:

```
WARN [AppPlugin] [protocol] package 'com.example.todo' declares no engines.protocol range;
loading under protocol 17.0.0 without a compatibility check (ADR-0087).
```

The same warning appears for the minimal fixture I wrote for #4084's e2e test, i.e. it is what *any* newly authored package gets.

## Why it matters

The examples are templates — people copy `objectstack.config.ts` out of them to start a project. An omission here propagates into every derived app, and each one silently opts out of the ADR-0087 compatibility check that exists to catch a package built against an older protocol major. The check is exactly the thing a v17 upgrade needs, and it is off by default in the apps we ship as the reference.

## Suggested fix

Declare an explicit `engines.protocol` range in `examples/app-todo`, `examples/app-crm`, and `examples/app-showcase` (and whatever `os init` scaffolds), so the shipped templates model the right thing. Worth deciding at the same time whether a package with no range should stay a warning or become a lint failure at `os compile` — the warning has been unobservable on both CLI entrypoints until now, so "nobody complained" carries no information.
